header.running_head: Enjoining what is Good and Forbidding what is Evil

blocks.text: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that on the day he was named Khalifah, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) sat on Rasulullaah ﷺ's pulpit. After duly praising Allaah and sending salutations to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he stretched out his hands and placed them on the spot of the pulpit where Rasulullaah ﷺ used to sit. He then said, "As he was sitting on this very same spot, I heard my beloved friend (Rasulullaah ﷺ) explain the meaning of the verse:

blocks.arabic_text: يٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِيْنَ اٰمَنُوْا عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ ۚ لَا يَضُرُّكُمْ مَّنْ ضَلَّ إِذَا اهْتَدَيْتُمْ
blocks.text: O you who have Imaan, take care of your own selves. He who has strayed cannot harm you when you are rightly guided.

In his explanation to us, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Yes. When evil is perpetrated in a community and they are being corrupted with vices without them making an attempt to change matters or to even oppose it, it becomes binding on Allaah to engulf them all in great punishment. Thereafter even their du'aas will not be accepted.'" Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then placed his fingers into his ears saying, "May both these ears become deaf if I had not heard this from my beloved friend (Rasulullaah ﷺ)."[^1]

Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "When people perpetrate evil in the midst of others who are more powerful than them but who do not prevent them, Allaah shall engulf them all in a great calamity that will not be alleviated."[^2]
Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) Instruct People to enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil

(Addressing the people) Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "When you people see a fool dishonouring people, what prevents you from opposing him?" When the people admitted that they feared abuse from the person, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "In that case, you will be unable to be witnesses (for the Ambiyaa on the Day of Qiyaamah)."[^3]

Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) once said, "Enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil before the worst amongst you are given authority over you and then when even the best of you make du'aa against them, their du'aas will not be accepted."[^4]
